newsitem.title: EGYPT: MIBANK plans five-for-one share split.
newsitem.headline: MIBANK plans five-for-one share split.

text.p: Shareholders in Egypt's Misr International Bank/MIBANK have approved a five-for-one share split to improve trading liquidity, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.

The bank has 4.5 million issued shares, some denominated in Egyptian pounds and others in dollars. At 750 pounds ($220) a share, the stock is bulky and the split would further stimulate trading, the official told Reuters.
"We have not yet set a date for the split but it has been approved and will happen shortly," he said.

The split reinforces a shake-up of the bank's activities. MIBANK is also planning to increase its capital and is vetting 10 global securities houses before offering its shares through a global depositary receipt.
Last June the board approved a one-for-two bonus issue and trading in the stock has since helped fuel the recent record highs on the Egyptian stock exchange.

State-run Banque Misr holds 44.8 percent of MIBANK and Misr Insurance four percent. Banca di Roma has 10 percent, Luxembourg-based Europartners Holdings 7.9, Sakura Bank Ltd of Japan 2.6 and British Arab Commercial Bank 8.5 percent. Individuals own the remaining 22.2 percent. ($=3.39 pounds) -- Miral Fahmy +202 578 3290/1
